subject: Re: Data access controls and support access - follow up
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>

Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial discovery - data handling & access controls

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning - it was helpful to understand Redwood's serving options. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec side and leadership:

- We need clarity on RBAC (roles, ability to enforce least privilege across tenants).
- Support & break-glass: what approvals/logging are in place when Redwood SREs access customer data?
- PII handling: retention defaults, deletion APIs, and ability to redact logs.
- Logging and audit trails: retention windows and proof of tamper-evidence.
- Data residency: can we pin to us-east for production?

I've attached FinTrust's standard security questionnaire - answered by our security team where relevant. Can you confirm which items Redwood can meet out-of-the-box vs. require an SOW?

(attachment: FinTrust_Security_Questionnaire.pdf [142KB])

Appreciate a short summary and next steps.

Best,
Olivia
Director of IT Risk
FinTrust

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - data handling & access controls

Hi Olivia -

Great to meet this morning. Thanks for sending the questionnaire - we've reviewed the items and here are the highlights specific to access controls and support access. See inline summary below and attached high-level RBAC overview.

TL;DR:
- RBAC: Role-based roles + custom roles; tenant scoping ensures least-privilege by default.
- Support access: time-limited break-glass with approval workflow + full audit logs and customer notification.
- PII & retention: configurable retention windows; deletion APIs and selective log redaction for PII.
- Logging: immutable audit trail for admin actions, 90-day default retention (extendable).
- Data residency: supported at region level (can pin to us-east for FT).

Quick answers to your bullets:
- RBAC: Built-in roles (Admin, Developer, ReadOnly) + custom roles. Policies are scoped to customers and can be applied at model/route level.
- Support & break-glass: Our support access requires a 2-stage approval (SRE on-call + account owner approval). Break-glass events trigger immediate audit logs, email notifications to designated security contacts, and a post-event report.
- PII handling: We provide configurable retention policies per customer and a deletion API that removes data from active stores and schedules background KV cache purge. We also offer optional PII redaction at ingestion.
- Logs & audit trail: Admin and support actions are logged with tamper-evident checksums; logs are exported to customer-owned storage (S3/GCS) on request.
- Residency: You can pin inference workloads and data at the region level; for production we support us-east pinning and can document controls in the contract.

Attachments: redwood_rbac_overview.pdf (high-level diagram + controls).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which questionnaire items you want completed as "standard" answers vs. requiring evidence (SOC2 report, architecture diagram).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Dev (cc'd) to walk through RBAC policies and the break-glass workflow.
3) If FinTrust needs extended log retention or managed SSO config assistance, we can scope in an SOW.

Would Thursday or Friday next week work for the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_rbac_overview.pdf [78KB])

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintrust.com>

Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - data handling & access controls

Marissa / Dev -

Thanks for the quick summary. A couple of clarifying Qs from our security team:  
- For break-glass, does the approval workflow have to be accepted by an FT account owner in our SSO, or can approvals be done via email? We prefer SSO-backed approvals where possible.
- We will need audit logs of any break-glass session (session start, initiator, approver, actions performed) retained for 365 days for high-risk accounts. Is that possible or would that be a paid retention add-on?
- For PII redaction: can redaction be applied retroactively to stored logs/metadata or only at ingestion?

Also - can you share SOC2 Type II and encryption-at-rest specifics (KMS / HSM usage)? If you can point us to the relevant docs we can mark items complete on our questionnaire.

Best,
Rajiv
Security Engineer
FinTrust

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery - data handling & access controls - next steps

Hi Olivia & Rajiv -

Thanks for the questions - quick responses and next steps below.

Responses:
- Approval workflow: We support SSO-backed approvals via SAML/SCIM integration (preferred) and can fall back to verified email approvals. We recommend SAML-based owner approval to ensure auditability.
- Log retention: 365-day retention for break-glass/audit logs is available as a subscription add-on (we'll include pricing in the SOW). Default is 90 days. Logs are exportable to customer-owned S3 buckets for long-term archival.
- Retroactive redaction: PII redaction is available at ingestion by default; retroactive redaction across archived logs requires a one-time job (can be scoped in the SOW).
- SOC2 & encryption: SOC2 Type II report and our encryption/KMS summary available - see links below.

Proposed immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
1) FinTrust to mark which questionnaire items need evidence vs. answers (Olivia/Rajiv).
2) Redwood to schedule a technical deep-dive (Dev) - proposed dates: Thu Mar 4 or Fri Mar 5.
3) Redwood to provide SOC2, KMS/HSM summary, detailed RBAC doc, and a draft SOW for extended retention + SSO assistance.

I'll have the pricing and SOW draft by EOD Wednesday. If that timeline works, we'll also prep the technical deep-dive agenda and sample config for SAML approvals.

Links and attachments: SOC2 Type II (redwood_security_report_2026.pdf) - shared via secure link after NDA. RBAC doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/rbac-overview

Thanks - looking forward to the deep-dive.

-Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
